facts.value: In most computers, individual instructions are stored as machine code with each instruction being given a unique number (its operation code or opcode for short). The command to add two numbers together would have one opcode; the command to multiply them would have a different opcode.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Computer Systems

facts.value: The simplest computers are able to perform any of a handful of different instructions; the more complex computers have several hundred to choose from, each with a unique numerical code.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Computer Systems

facts.value: Since the computer's memory is able to store numbers, it can also store the instruction codes.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Computer Systems

facts.value: Entire programs can be represented as lists of numbers and can themselves be manipulated inside the computer in the same way as numeric data.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Computer Systems

facts.value: The fundamental concept of storing programs in the computer's memory alongside the data they operate on is the crux of the von Neumann, or stored program, architecture.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Computer Systems

facts.value: In some cases, a computer might store some or all of its program in memory that is kept separate from the data it operates on, which is called the Harvard architecture.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Computer Systems

facts.value: Modern von Neumann computers display some traits of the Harvard architecture in their designs, such as in CPU caches.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Computer Systems

facts.value: While it is possible to write computer programs as long lists of numbers (machine language), it is extremely tedious and potentially error-prone to do so in practice, especially for complicated programs.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Computer Systems

facts.value: Instead, each basic instruction can be given a short name that is indicative of its function and easy to remember, such as ADD, SUB, MULT or JUMP.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Computer Systems

facts.value: These mnemonics are collectively known as a computer's assembly language.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Computer Systems

facts.value: Converting programs written in assembly language into something the computer can actually understand (machine language) is usually done by a computer program called an assembler.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Computer Systems
